question.text: A group of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn></math> students appeared in an examination of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math> subjects - Mathematics, Physics & Chemistry. It was found that all students passed in at least one of the subjects, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn></math> students passed in Mathematics, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn></math> students passed in Physics, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>16</mn></math> students passed in Chemistry, at most <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn></math> students passed in both Mathematics and Physics, at most <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn></math> students passed in both Physics and Chemistry, at most <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn></math> students passed in both Mathematics and Chemistry. The maximum number of students passed in all the three subjects is _____.
